name: AppFooter
description: The footer of an application or marketing page: a line of text, link lists and social links. It stacks on a phone and has the same size and spacing on every page.

text.description: The text on the left, usually the copyright line.

links.description: Footer links: a flat list of { label, href }, or groups of { title, links } for the columns layout.

social.description: Social links, such as icon buttons. Give each one an accessible name.

layout.description: simple is one row; columns lists each group under its heading.

navLabel.description: Name of the footer navigation landmark.

renderLink.description: Draw links as your router's link. Return the link with the given className and children.
renderLink.tsType: (props: { link: import("../app-footer/links").FooterLink; className: string; children: import("react").ReactNode }) => import("react").ReactNode

classNames.description: Extra class names for single parts, so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Keys: root, inner, text, nav, group, groupTitle, list, link, social.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the links, then the social slot
requirements: The footer is the page's contentinfo landmark; use one per page
The links sit in a navigation landmark with its own name ("Footer" by default)
In the columns layout each group has a real heading, so people can jump between groups
Links to other sites that open in a new tab say so to screen readers
screenReader: "Product, heading level 2", then its links as a list

use_when: The bottom of an application shell, a marketing page or an auth screen
avoid_when: Page-level actions or pagination: those belong in the page
anti_patterns: Different padding or width on each page: use the footer as it is and restyle it once through classNames
More than one footer on a page

contract.data: Link groups as plain { label, href } objects, and a text line.
